attempted_claim: Let L be a non-split link with Turaev genus 1, with integral Khovanov homology Kh^{i,j}(L), extremal quantum gradings j_min(L), j_max(L), and signature sigma(L). Prove or disprove: either Kh^{*,j_min(L)}(L) = Kh^{i_0,j_min(L)}(L) ≅ Z with 2i_0 − j_min(L) = sigma(L)+1, or Kh^{*,j_max(L)}(L) = Kh^{i_0,j_max(L)}(L) ≅ Z with 2i_0 − j_max(L) = sigma(L)−1.
decisive_failure: Rank-level KnotAtlas tables cannot detect integral torsion at extremal gradings, so the survey constrains but does not decide the target. Signature values were taken from KnotTheory computer-talk output with a trefoil-calibrated sign convention rather than an independent Goeritz computation. The integral chain-complex toolkit was incomplete, and no general proof argument was constructed; torsion-hunt candidates with a failing max side remain untested.
